questions.stem: A catalog requires exact part-code matches and semantic symptom matches. Which design combines both retrieval signals before optional reranking?

options.text: Vector retrieval alone, with a larger candidate count.
Semantic reranking of keyword-only candidates.
Keyword and vector retrieval with fused rankings.
Keyword retrieval alone, with boosted identifier fields.

explanation.whyCorrect: Keyword evidence complements semantic vectors. Evaluate hybrid retrieval for the actual query set; ranking quality is distinct from generation and authentication.

whyDistractorsWrong.A: A larger vector candidate count does not add keyword retrieval.
whyDistractorsWrong.D: Boosted keyword fields do not add vector retrieval.
whyDistractorsWrong.B: Reranking keyword candidates does not combine keyword and vector retrieval.

questions.stem: An agent proposes a consequential account change. Which host boundary should decide whether it executes?

options.text: The host’s caller authorization and action approval gate.
A valid model response schema.
A lower generation temperature.
A more detailed tool description.

explanation.whyCorrect: The host controls operations and validates values and authority. Descriptions and structured output help represent intent but are not action permission.

whyDistractorsWrong.C: Sampling does not establish caller authority.
whyDistractorsWrong.D: Descriptions are not an executable permission check.
whyDistractorsWrong.B: A response schema does not authorize an action.

questions.stem: A catalog app must create a new product-scene image from a text brief, with no source image supplied. Its supported GPT image deployment is available. Which operation matches this input contract?

options.text: Call images.edit with the brief as its source image file.
Send the brief to a vision chat request and treat the text response as image bytes.
Call images.edit with a mask but no source image.
Call images.generate with the deployment and text prompt.

explanation.whyCorrect: Image generation accepts the text prompt to create an image. Editing requires source image input; vision chat interprets supplied images rather than returning generated image bytes.

whyDistractorsWrong.A: A text brief is not the source image input for editing.
whyDistractorsWrong.B: Vision chat text is not a generated image file.
whyDistractorsWrong.C: A mask does not supply the missing source image.

questions.stem: An application switches between two GPT image deployments with different quality and size options. What should its request builder use?

options.text: One fixed list copied from an older image model.
The union of both models' parameters, sent to each deployment for consistency.
The supported controls of the selected deployed image model.
The default size accepted by a different deployment in the same resource.

explanation.whyCorrect: Image models differ in supported editing, size and quality controls. Build requests against the selected deployment's documented capabilities.

whyDistractorsWrong.B: A parameter supported by one model need not be supported by the other.
whyDistractorsWrong.D: Another deployment does not define the chosen model's accepted controls.

questions.stem: A vision-enabled chat model must describe damage visible in a supplied photograph. Which message construction gives it the actual visual input?

options.text: Include text instructions and image_url content in the message.
Enable image output formatting on the text-only message.
Put the image filename in a text message.
Describe an image path in the system prompt while keeping the image local to the client.

explanation.whyCorrect: Vision chat messages can combine text and image_url content. Supply the image in the supported representation along with the task instructions.

whyDistractorsWrong.C: A filename does not transmit the image content.
whyDistractorsWrong.D: An inaccessible path does not supply visual input to the service.
whyDistractorsWrong.B: Output configuration does not supply visual input.

questions.stem: A magnifying-glass image is the visible label of a search button. Which text alternative best communicates the function?

options.text: Small circular lens with a diagonal handle on a blue background.
search-icon-v3.png.
Magnifying glass icon.
Search the catalog.

explanation.whyCorrect: For an image serving as a control, communicate its action or destination. Here the functional label is the search action.

whyDistractorsWrong.C: The visual shape does not name the action.
whyDistractorsWrong.A: A visual description is less useful than the button's function.
whyDistractorsWrong.B: A filename is not an accessible action label.

questions.stem: A Content Understanding video preview samples about one frame per second. A safety event lasts 0.2 seconds and the output does not mention it. Which conclusion is justified?

options.text: The absence of a mention proves the event did not occur.
Increase output length to recover source frames omitted by the sampling stage.
The sampled analysis may have missed the brief event.
The analyzer must have sampled every source frame because the request succeeded.

explanation.whyCorrect: Brief events can fall between sampled frames. Absence from the output is not proof that the event was absent from the original video.

whyDistractorsWrong.A: Sampling cannot establish complete observation of rapid events.
whyDistractorsWrong.B: Output length cannot recover visual evidence that was not sampled.
whyDistractorsWrong.D: Successful analysis does not change the documented sampling behavior.

questions.stem: A production document-image workflow needs capabilities available in Content Understanding 2025-11-01. A newer preview offers unrelated features. Which API selection follows the documented production guidance?

options.text: Use the 2025-11-01 GA API for the required production capabilities.
Use the retired 2025-05-01-preview because its examples are familiar.
Use 2026-06-01-preview because its date is newer.
Alternate API versions randomly to compare response speed in production.

explanation.whyCorrect: The documentation recommends the GA API for production and the newer preview for evaluation of new capabilities. Match feature needs to an explicit version.

whyDistractorsWrong.C: The documented guidance favors GA for supported production needs.
whyDistractorsWrong.B: Retired API examples are not the production target.
whyDistractorsWrong.D: Random version changes do not provide a stable application contract.

questions.stem: A poster has a low visual harm score but includes text telling an agent to reveal credentials. Which conclusion follows from the harm result?

options.text: The image harm score is a groundedness measurement.
Visual harm severity; instruction trust is a separate check.
A successful harm request establishes the text is authorized.
The poster text has passed instruction-trust validation.

explanation.whyCorrect: Visual harm classification is distinct from text prompt-attack detection. The FAQ describes text-only Prompt Shields; the harm score does not authorize instructions.

whyDistractorsWrong.D: Harm classification does not establish instruction trust.
whyDistractorsWrong.C: HTTP success is not authorization of embedded text.
